mainTopic: The source that מעשר בהמה may not be sold (from חרמים, and רב אשי's reading of ״לא יגאל״), and the dispute over whether non-כהנים may eat a blemished בכור.
overview: The גמרא looks for a source that a מעשר בהמה animal may not be sold. The first approach says the words ״לא יגאל״ written by חרמים are extra there, so they teach about מעשר. They go to מעשר and not to בכור because the Torah uses the word גאולה by מעשר, just like by חרמים. רב אשי gives a different source: the ״לא יגאל״ written by מעשר itself means 'it may not be sold.' He proves this because the verse links ״לא יגאל״ to תמורה, which works only while the animal is alive, and redeeming a slaughtered animal makes no sense. The גמרא defends this proof against two challenges, using a קל וחומר: if strong, living holiness cannot be redeemed, weaker holiness after slaughter certainly cannot. The Torah wrote ״לא יגאל״ instead of ״לא ימכר״ to forbid both selling and redeeming. Then a new משנה brings a dispute: בית שמאי say only כהנים may eat a blemished בכור, while בית הלל permit a ישראל and even a גוי. The גמרא shows that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, and explains that בית שמאי learn their view from a verse comparing the בכור to the חזה ושוק, which only כהנים may eat.

steps.title: Why does the Torah need the extra words 'it shall not be redeemed'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Torah wrote ״לא יגאל״ in the חרמים verse, since it seems unnecessary there.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...be redeemed' that the Torah wrote, why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the words ״לא יגאל״ in the חרמים verse and asks what they are there for. This sets up the next move, where the extra words will be put to use somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are treated as extra, because what they teach about חרמים is already known from another source. In גמרא logic, extra words in a פסוק are not wasted. They are moved to teach a law about a different topic.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah / ה׳
Why do I need it? (a sign that a word looks extra)

phrases.english: '...be redeemed' that the Merciful One wrote
phrases.notes: This amud begins mid-quote. The full phrase is ״ולא יגאל״ from the חרמים verse (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״ח), which says 'it shall not be sold and it shall not be redeemed.'

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf about the source for not selling מעשר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the purpose of the seemingly extra ״לא יגאל״ by חרמים?

steps.title: Apply the extra words to the animal tithe
steps.stepSummary: Since the words are not needed for חרמים, they are moved over to teach about מעשר: it may not be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is not needed for the topic of חרמים, apply it to the topic of מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra words are moved over to teach about מעשר בהמה. The result is that מעשר, like חרמים, may not be sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the standard method called 'אם אינו ענין'. If a phrase is not needed in its own topic, it teaches about another topic. The link between the topics is the word ״לא יגאל״, which appears in both places. Because the חרמים verse says 'not sold' right next to 'not redeemed', the 'not sold' rule carries over to מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for its own topic
Property dedicated with a חרם vow
Here: מעשר בהמה, the tithe of animals

phrases.english: If it is not needed for the matter of dedications,
apply it to the matter of the animal tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לַחֲרָמִים תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra ״לא יגאל״ teaches that מעשר may not be sold.

steps.title: Why not apply it to the firstborn instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the extra words go to מעשר and not to בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: apply it to the topic of בכור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the choice of מעשר. Maybe the extra words should teach a law about בכור instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra word can only be moved to one topic. So the גמרא needs a reason why it goes to מעשר rather than to another holy animal like בכור. This challenge sets up the next step's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal, given to the כהן

phrases.english: Say instead: apply it to the matter of a firstborn?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to apply the extra words to מעשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing so far shows why מעשר is preferred over בכור.

steps.title: The tithe shares the word 'redemption' with dedications
steps.stepSummary: מעשר is chosen because the Torah uses redemption language (״לא יגאל״) by מעשר, just as by חרמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעשר has 'redemption' written by it, just like חרמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that מעשר is the better match. The same word, גאולה, is written by both מעשר and חרמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared wording connects the two topics. That shared wording is not found the same way by בכור. So the extra words are applied to the topic that 'looks like' חרמים.
steps.whatToRemember: First approach: ״לא יגאל״ by חרמים is extra, so it teaches that מעשר may not be sold. מעשר is chosen over בכור because both מעשר and חרמים use the word גאולה.

phrases.english: The tithe has 'redemption' written by it, just like it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shared wording links מעשר to חרמים more closely than בכור.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra words could just as well teach about בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra words go to מעשר, because מעשר shares the term גאולה with חרמים.

steps.title: רב אשי: 'not redeemed' by the tithe means 'not sold'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers a different source: the ״לא יגאל״ in the מעשר verse itself means 'it may not be sold.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: ״לא יגאל״ written by מעשר means 'it may not be sold.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new source for the same law. He does not need חרמים at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of borrowing words from חרמים, רב אשי reads the מעשר verse itself in a new way. The word 'redeem' there means 'sell'. This is a different way to reach the same conclusion that מעשר may not be sold.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read ״לא יגאל״ here in its normal meaning of redemption. רב אשי's whole point is that in the מעשר verse, this word means selling.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
'It shall not be redeemed' of the tithe
means: it shall not be sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative source to the אם אינו ענין derivation from חרמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ״לא יגאל״ in the מעשר verse means 'may not be sold.'

steps.title: רב אשי brings the verse about the tithe and its substitute
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes the מעשר verse, which places תמורה right next to ״לא יגאל״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: How do I know this? Because it is written: 'Then both it and its substitute shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי starts proving his reading by quoting the פסוק. This sets up the reasoning in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point is that the verse puts תמורה and ״לא יגאל״ side by side. Because they are next to each other, רב אשי will compare the two laws.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this?
Substitute: an animal swapped for a holy one, which also becomes holy

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
From where do I say this?
As it is written: 'Then both it and its substitute
shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed' (Leviticus 27:33).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the proof for רב אשי's statement in step 5.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא כ״ז:ל״ג, where תמורה and ״לא יגאל״ appear together.

steps.title: Literal redemption would be impossible after slaughter
steps.stepSummary: תמורה works only while the animal is alive, so ״לא יגאל״ should also apply only while it is alive. That would mean redemption is allowed after slaughter, but redemption needs העמדה והערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does it make a תמורה? While alive. When may it not be redeemed? While alive. So after slaughter it may be redeemed? But redemption requires standing the animal up and valuing it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows that reading ״לא יגאל״ literally leads to an impossible result. The verse links it to תמורה, which applies only while the animal is alive. So 'not redeemed' should also apply only while alive, which would mean you could redeem a slaughtered animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming a holy animal requires העמדה והערכה: the animal must stand before a כהן so he can value it. A slaughtered animal cannot stand. So 'redemption after slaughter' makes no sense. This is a proof by contradiction against the literal reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing the animal up and valuing it (needed for redemption)

phrases.english: When does it make a substitute? While alive.
When may it not be redeemed? While alive.
This implies that after slaughter it may be redeemed.
But redemption requires standing and valuation!
phrases.notes: A slaughtered animal cannot be stood up and valued (see ויקרא כ״ז:י״א–י״ב).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Develops the proof from the verse quoted in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The literal reading of ״לא יגאל״ cannot be right.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The link between תמורה and ״לא יגאל״, together with the rule that redemption needs העמדה והערכה.

steps.title: Conclusion: 'not redeemed' means 'not sold'
steps.stepSummary: Since literal redemption makes no sense, ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר must mean that the animal may not be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: 'it shall not be redeemed' means 'it shall not be sold.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי concludes his proof. The word in the verse means 'sold', not 'redeemed'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the literal meaning ruled out, 'sale' fits the verse. Selling a slaughtered animal is possible, so the comparison to תמורה now works: the ban on selling applies while the animal is alive, and after slaughter it may be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this / conclude from this

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי: ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר means 'not sold.' He proves it because literal redemption would have to be allowed after slaughter, which is impossible without העמדה והערכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a second, independent source for the ban on selling מעשר. It also limits that ban to the time the animal is alive, just like תמורה.

phrases.english: Rather, conclude from this:
'it shall not be redeemed' means: it shall not be sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the impossibility shown in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the מעשר verse, ״לא יגאל״ means 'may not be sold'. The ban applies while the animal is alive.

steps.title: רב אשי's proof only works for one opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's proof. The argument that a slaughtered animal cannot be redeemed because it cannot stand for העמדה והערכה only works for the view that קדשי מזבח needed העמדה והערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says that altar-consecrated animals were included in the rule of 'standing and valuation.' But for the one who says they were NOT included in that rule, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in step 7 of רב אשי's proof. It says that proof depends on one side of a known מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said that after slaughter, redemption is impossible because a dead animal cannot be stood up and valued (העמדה והערכה). But some hold that blemished קדשי מזבח never needed העמדה והערכה in the first place. By that view, a slaughtered מעשר could be redeemed, so ״לא יגאל״ could mean literal redemption after all.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (opens a challenge against another view)
Animals consecrated to be offered on the altar
Included in the requirement that the animal be stood up and valued before redemption
What is there to say? (the other view has a problem)

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה,
phrases.english: altar-consecrated animals were included in 'standing and valuation,'
but according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ לֹא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה,
phrases.english: altar-consecrated animals were NOT included in 'standing and valuation,'
what is there to say?
phrases.notes: By this view, redemption after slaughter is possible, so the literal meaning could stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the העמדה והערכה premise used in step 7 to reach step 8's conclusion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that redemption after slaughter is impossible because of העמדה והערכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The premise is disputed. By the view that קדשי מזבח need no העמדה והערכה, a slaughtered animal could be redeemed, so ״לא יגאל״ could be taken literally.

steps.title: The real argument: no redemption after slaughter if none while alive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the proof was never based on העמדה והערכה alone. The point is that it makes no sense for an animal to be unredeemable while alive but redeemable after slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we meant: is there any case where an animal cannot be redeemed while alive, yet can be redeemed after slaughter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by clarifying what the argument really is. The argument is logical and works for every opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof now rests on simple logic, not on the העמדה והערכה rule. If ״לא יגאל״ applies only while the animal is alive, then redemption would only become possible after slaughter. Such a backwards result is unheard of, so the literal reading fails for both opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we meant (clarifying an earlier argument)
It is redeemed / can be redeemed

phrases.english: This is what we were saying:
is there anything that cannot be redeemed while alive,
and yet can be redeemed after slaughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by changing the basis of the proof from העמדה והערכה to general logic.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אשי's proof depended on the העמדה והערכה requirement and so fails for the other opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: The proof depends on logic: something unredeemable while alive cannot become redeemable after slaughter.

steps.title: Maybe weaker sanctity after slaughter allows redemption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Perhaps it does make sense: while alive the sanctity is strong, so no redemption, but after slaughter the sanctity is weaker, so redemption is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? While alive, when its holiness is strong, it cannot be redeemed. After slaughter, when its holiness is weaker, it can be redeemed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the logic of step 10. It offers a reason why redemption might be allowed only after slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge argues that holiness weakens after slaughter. Weaker holiness should be easier to remove through redemption. If so, the 'backwards' scenario is reasonable, and ״לא יגאל״ could be literal again.

phrases.english: Why not?
While alive, when its holiness is strong, it is not redeemed;

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה דְּאַקֵּיל לֵיהּ קְדוּשְׁתֵּיהּ — מִיפְּרִיק!
phrases.english: after slaughter, when its holiness has weakened, it is redeemed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logical claim of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that redemption after slaughter alone is unreasonable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Weaker sanctity after slaughter could explain why redemption becomes possible only then.

steps.title: A קל וחומר shows the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge with a קל וחומר. Strong sanctity is better able to pass into money. If even strong, living sanctity cannot be redeemed, then weak sanctity after slaughter certainly cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it all the more so the other way? While alive, when it is strong enough to pass its holiness onto its redemption money, it cannot be redeemed. After slaughter, when it is not strong enough to pass its holiness onto its redemption money, should it be redeemable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the challenge around. It shows that weaker sanctity makes redemption harder, not easier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redemption works by moving holiness from the animal onto the money. A living animal has the power to transfer holiness, as we see from תמורה. A slaughtered one loses that power. So if the stronger, living animal still cannot be redeemed, the weaker slaughtered one certainly cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so (a קל וחומר)
To 'grab' or take hold of, meaning to transfer holiness onto something

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think weaker holiness is easier to redeem. Here the גמרא says redemption needs strong holiness, because the holiness must be strong enough to pass onto the money.

phrases.english: But isn't it all the more so (the other way)?

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה מֵחַיִּים דְּאַלִּים לְמִיתְפַּס פִּדְיוֹנוֹ — לָא מִיפְּרִיק,
phrases.english: If while alive, when it is strong enough to transfer holiness to its redemption money, it is not redeemed,

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה דְּלָא אַלִּים לְמִיתְפָּס פִּדְיוֹנוֹ — מִיפְּרִיק?
phrases.english: then after slaughter, when it is not strong enough to transfer holiness to its redemption money, should it be redeemed?
phrases.notes: Proof of strength: a living animal can make a תמורה, but a slaughtered one cannot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 11's challenge with a reverse קל וחומר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that weakened sanctity after slaughter permits redemption
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Redemption depends on the power to transfer sanctity, and that power is weaker after slaughter, so redemption should be even less possible.

steps.title: Conclusion: ״לא יגאל״ means 'not sold'
steps.stepSummary: Since literal redemption cannot fit the verse, the גמרא concludes that ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר means the animal may not be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: 'It may not be redeemed' means 'it may not be sold.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the defense of רב אשי. His reading stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the attacks on רב אשי's argument have been answered. Literal redemption makes no sense in the verse, so ״לא יגאל״ must refer to selling.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this / conclude from this

steps.whatToRemember: ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר בהמה means 'not sold.' This holds for every opinion, because the proof is logical: something unredeemable while alive cannot become redeemable after slaughter.

phrases.english: Rather, conclude from this:
'It may not be redeemed' means 'it may not be sold.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates step 8's conclusion now that the challenges are resolved.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר means it may not be sold.

steps.title: Why not simply write 'not sold'?
steps.stepSummary: If the verse means 'not sold,' the גמרא asks why the Torah did not just write ״לא ימכר״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the Torah write 'it may not be sold'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the word choice of the פסוק. Why use a word that means redemption if the meaning is selling?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that ״לא יגאל״ is read as 'not sold,' the Torah's wording seems indirect. The Torah normally says things plainly, so the different word must teach something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let the Merciful One (the Torah) write

phrases.english: Then let the Merciful One write 'It may not be sold'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the verse based on step 13's conclusion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Torah's choice of ״לא יגאל״ for a ban on selling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the meaning is 'not sold,' the plainer word ״לא ימכר״ should have been used.

steps.title: ״לא יגאל״ forbids both selling and redeeming
steps.stepSummary: Had the Torah written ״לא ימכר״, we would forbid only selling, since selling treats the holy animal like ordinary property. We might still allow redemption, since the money becomes holy. ״לא יגאל״ forbids both.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had written 'it may not be sold,' I would say only selling is forbidden, because that treats it like an ordinary item. But redeeming would be allowed, because its money goes to הקדש. That is why the Torah wrote 'it may not be redeemed': it may not be sold and it may not be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the word ״לא יגאל״ was chosen to cover two bans at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling is clearly worse, because it treats the holy animal as ordinary property and the money stays ordinary. Redemption seems more acceptable, since the money becomes holy. The word ״לא יגאל״ teaches that even redemption is forbidden, and selling is forbidden as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Acts of the non-holy; treating something like ordinary property
Its money goes into הקדש (becomes holy)

steps.whatToRemember: By מעשר בהמה, ״לא יגאל״ teaches two bans: no selling and no redeeming.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the Torah's wording. It also sets the הלכה that מעשר בהמה cannot be redeemed, and cannot be sold while it is alive, even after it gets a blemish.

phrases.english: If the Merciful One had written 'It may not be sold,'
I would have said:
it is only selling that it may not be sold,
because he is treating it like ordinary property,
but as for redemption, it can be redeemed,
since its money goes into הקדש.
Therefore the Merciful One wrote 'It may not be redeemed,'
teaching that it may not be sold
and it may not be redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִמָּכֵר״ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14's question about the Torah's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Wording teaches an extra law (הוה אמינא resolved)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With ״לא ימכר״ alone, redemption would be allowed because the money becomes holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״לא יגאל״ forbids both selling and redeeming.

steps.title: New משנה: may a non-priest share in a blemished firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה records a dispute. בית שמאי forbid a ישראל from being counted with a כהן to eat a בכור. בית הלל permit it, even for a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say a ישראל may not be counted together with a כהן to eat the בכור. בית הלל permit it, and they permit it even for a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic. It asks whether a non-כהן may join a כהן in eating a בכור that has a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a בכור gets a blemish (מום), it is given to the כהן and may be eaten outside the ביהמ"ק. The question is whether it stays limited to כהנים like a regular קרבן. בית שמאי say only כהנים may eat it. בית הלל say anyone may, even a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male kosher animal, given to the כהן
Be counted, meaning signed up as one of the group eating the animal

steps.confusionAlert: This is about a בכור that has a blemish (בעל מום), not an unblemished בכור offered on the מזבח. The משנה doesn't say this outright, but the context of the פרק makes it clear.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִמָּנֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל עִם הַכֹּהֵן לַבְּכוֹר,
phrases.english: An Israelite may not be counted with the priest for the firstborn,
phrases.notes: 'Counted' means joining the group that will eat the animal.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel permit it,
and even a gentile.
phrases.notes: The גמרא will show that this clause follows רבי עקיבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is unrelated to the preceding discussion of מעשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: only כהנים may eat a blemished בכור. בית הלל: even a ישראל, and even a גוי.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה follows, especially its phrase 'even a גוי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who wrote the משנה's version of בית הלל. This sets up the next step, where it will identify the author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'even a גוי' is a surprising extension of בית הלל's view. The גמרא wants to know which תנא reports בית הלל this way.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
Whose opinion is our Mishnah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who authored the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that בית הלל permit even a גוי to eat a blemished בכור.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא, as a ברייתא shows
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the same dispute. In it, רבי עקיבא is the one who says בית הלל permit even a גוי. So the משנה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי עקיבא, as a ברייתא teaches: a בכור may be eaten only by a group made up entirely of כהנים. These are the words of בית שמאי. בית הלל say: even non-כהנים. רבי עקיבא permits even a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. It proves this from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the regular version of בית הלל says only 'even זרים' (non-כהנים). It is רבי עקיבא who adds 'even a גוי.' Since our משנה includes 'even a גוי,' it must follow רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
A group that eats a קרבן together

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's phrase 'even a גוי' is not the plain view of בית הלל. It is רבי עקיבא's way of reporting בית הלל.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Akiva,
as it is taught in a baraita:
For a firstborn, one may not be counted on it
except a group made up entirely of priests,
these are the words of Beit Shammai.
And Beit Hillel say: even non-priests.
Rabbi Akiva permits even a gentile.
phrases.notes: This matches the משנה's final words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of who authored the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who extends בית הלל's permission even to a גוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא recording the dispute, with רבי עקיבא's addition.

steps.title: What is בית שמאי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of בית שמאי's rule that only כהנים may eat a blemished בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks why בית שמאי forbid non-כהנים. This sets up the verse brought in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished בכור may be eaten outside the ביהמ"ק, so it seems almost like ordinary meat. The גמרא wants to know what source keeps it limited to כהנים.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Beit Shammai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After identifying the author, the גמרא turns to the reasoning behind בית שמאי's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for limiting a blemished בכור to כהנים.

steps.title: The firstborn is compared to the breast and thigh
steps.stepSummary: The verse says the בכור's meat is 'yours' like the חזה ושוק. Only כהנים eat the חזה ושוק, so only כהנים may eat the בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And their meat shall be yours, etc.' Just as there, כהנים may eat and ישראלים may not, so too here, כהנים may eat and ישראלים may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית שמאי's source. It is a verse that compares the בכור's meat to the breast and thigh, which only כהנים may eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full verse reads: 'their meat shall be yours, like the breast of waving and the right thigh.' Since the חזה ושוק are eaten only by כהנים and their families, בית שמאי say the בכור's meat must also stay with כהנים, even after it gets a blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And their meat shall be yours' (במדבר י"ח:י"ח)

steps.confusionAlert: The comparison is hidden in 'וגו׳' (etc.). The rest of the verse says 'like the חזה התנופה and the שוק הימין.' That missing part is what 'there' refers to.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי limit a blemished בכור to כהנים because the verse compares it to the חזה ושוק, which only כהנים may eat.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And their flesh shall be yours, etc."
phrases.notes: The verse continues: 'like the wave breast and the right thigh.'

phrases.english: Just as there, priests: yes,
Israelites: no,
so too here, priests: yes,
Israelites: no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about בית שמאי's reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse compares the בכור's meat to the חזה ושוק. Like them, it may be eaten only by כהנים.
